title: Two-Tier Image Cache: Memory + Disk
hints: Check memory, then disk, then the network, in that order.
On a disk hit, put the value into memory; on a network hit, write to both.
Purging memory simulates a relaunch: the next `get` should hit disk.
jsBridge: Memory cache first, then disk, then network, as an actor to coordinate concurrent requests. It's how Kingfisher/Nuke (and browser HTTP caches) work, with the actor serialising cache state.

compass.q: The browser gives you memory + disk HTTP caches for free. What must an iOS app implement itself for decoded images?
Disk cache growth: when and how do you evict (size limit, age)? Which folder (Caches) can iOS purge?
Your own cache vs `URLCache` vs Kingfisher/Nuke: when is rolling your own justified?
Hash URLs for file names: why SHA-256 and not `hashValue`?
